guide.summary: Some syllables change tone because of the tone that follows. 不 and 一 switch depending on the next syllable, a 3rd tone before another 3rd tone rises like a 2nd, and before any other tone it just stays low. Always look one syllable ahead. Pinyin here shows 不 and 一 as spoken (bú, yí, yì) but keeps the written 3rd-tone mark (nǐ hǎo, said ní hǎo).

subs.label: 不 becomes bú before a 4th tone
subs.focus: 不 directly before a 4th-tone syllable (是, 去, 要, 会, 对, 太, 用, 错, 客气, 看). Learner must pick bú, not bù. Classic error: keeping the dictionary tone and saying bù shì, bù yào with two falling tones in a row.

subs.label: 不 stays bù, or goes light in the middle
subs.focus: 不 before a 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone or alone stays bù (bù chī, bù lái, bù hǎo); inside V不V and V不complement it is light (shì bu shì, tīng bu dǒng). Error: over-applying bú everywhere (bú hǎo, bú zhī dao). Decide by the next syllable's tone.

subs.label: 一 becomes yí before a 4th tone
subs.focus: 一 counting something, before a 4th-tone syllable or 个 (一个, 一样, 一定, 一共, 一下, 一次, 一块, 一会儿, 一件, 一万). Learner must pick yí. Errors: citation yī ge, or yì used for every changed 一.

subs.label: 一 becomes yì before 1st, 2nd, 3rd tones
subs.focus: 一 before a 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone (一天, 一些, 一杯, 一年, 一直, 一条, 一起, 一点儿, 一本, 一百). Learner must pick yì, not yī and not yí. Error: yī qǐ, yī tiān, or yí nián by analogy with yí ge.

subs.label: 一 stays yī as a number name
subs.focus: 一 read as a digit or ordinal keeps yī whatever follows: counting, end of phrase, 第一, 十一, 二十一, 一月, 一号, 星期一, years. Also light 一 in V一V (kàn yi kàn). Error: yí yuè, dì yí cì, shí yí ge. Contrast 一月 with 一个月. Avoid 一点 for one o'clock (variable).

subs.label: 3rd + 3rd: the first rises
subs.focus: Two adjacent 3rd tones in one word or phrase (你好, 很好, 可以, 水果, 老板, 所以, 手表, 我想). Learner must identify that the first is said as a 2nd tone while the spelling keeps both marks. Error: two full dipping tones, or changing the second instead of the first.

subs.label: Three or more 3rd tones in a row
subs.focus: Runs of three or four 3rd tones (我很好, 老板也来, 我有五本). Learner groups by word or phrase, changes the first of each pair, and keeps the last one before a pause as 3rd. Error: changing none, or changing only the first syllable. Accept the fast all-rising variant.

subs.label: 3rd tone before other tones stays low
subs.focus: A 3rd tone before a 1st, 2nd, 4th or neutral syllable (老师, 很忙, 好看, 我的, 喜欢) is low with no final rise and does NOT turn into a 2nd tone. Error: full dip-and-rise mid-sentence, or over-applying the rising change (hén máng). Full 3rd only alone or before a pause.

subs.label: Neutral tone: particles and doubled words
subs.focus: Which syllable is light: particles (的, 了, 吗, 呢, 吧, 着, 过), suffixes 子 and 们, the second half of doubled kin terms and verbs (妈妈, 谢谢, 看看, 想想). Error: full tone on both halves (mā mā, kàn kàn), or making 天天, 常常, 人人 light when they keep their tones.

rules.rule: 不 is normally bù (4th tone). Right before another 4th tone it rises to bú, so you never say two falling tones on 不 + word.

examples.en: I'm not a student.

examples.py: míng tiān wǒ bú qù gōng sī
examples.en: I'm not going to the office tomorrow.

examples.py: zhè jiàn yī fu bú tài guì
examples.en: This piece of clothing isn't too expensive.
You're welcome!

rules.note: Dictionaries and many textbooks still print bù in every word (bùshì, bùyào). The spoken tone is bú all the same.

rules.rule: Before a 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone, and when 不 stands alone or ends the phrase, it keeps its own 4th tone: bù.

examples.en: I don't eat meat.

examples.py: tā jīn tiān bù lái le
examples.en: He's not coming today after all.

examples.py: zhè ge bàn fǎ bù hǎo
examples.en: This method is no good.
No, I'm not going.

rules.rule: Sandwiched in the middle of verb-不-verb questions and verb-不-result forms, 不 is short and light with no tone of its own.
rules.pattern: Verb + 不 (bu) + Verb; Verb + 不 (bu) + result

examples.py: nǐ shì bu shì lǎo shī
examples.en: Are you a teacher?
I can't understand (what I hear).

examples.py: duì bu qǐ wǒ lái wǎn le
examples.en: Sorry, I'm late.

rules.note: In slow, careful speech the tone can come back; then the normal rule applies (shì bú shì, tīng bù dǒng). Both are heard; light is the everyday default.

rules.rule: When 一 counts or modifies what follows and the next syllable is 4th tone, say yí (rising). 个 counts as 4th tone even though it is usually said lightly.

examples.py: wǒ yǒu yí ge dì di
examples.en: I have a younger brother.
Please wait a moment.

examples.py: zhè liǎng ge zì de yì si yí yàng
examples.en: These two characters mean the same thing.

examples.py: wǒ men yí gòng wǔ ge rén
examples.en: There are five of us altogether.

rules.rule: Before a 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone, 一 drops to yì (falling).

examples.py: tā yì tiān hē sān bēi kā fēi
examples.en: He drinks three cups of coffee a day.

examples.py: wǒ xué le yì nián hàn yǔ
examples.en: I studied Chinese for a year.

examples.py: wǒ men yì qǐ qù ba
examples.en: Let's go together.

examples.py: wǒ huì shuō yì diǎn r hàn yǔ
examples.en: I can speak a little Chinese.

rules.note: 一百 and 一千 follow this rule (yì bǎi, yì qiān) and 一万 follows the 4th-tone rule (yí wàn), because 一 is counting the unit after it.

rules.rule: When 一 is read as a number name it keeps yī whatever comes next: counting, ordinals with 第, the last digit of a number, dates and weekdays, and at the end of a phrase.
rules.pattern: 第 + 一 (yī); 十 + 一 (yī); 一 (yī) + 月 / 号; 星期 + 一 (yī)

examples.py: zhè shì wǒ dì yī cì lái zhōng guó
examples.en: This is my first time in China.

examples.zh: 我们班有二十一个学生。
examples.py: wǒ men bān yǒu èr shí yī ge xué sheng
examples.en: There are twenty-one students in our class.

examples.py: tā de shēng rì shì yī yuè yī hào
examples.en: His birthday is the first of January.
Today is Monday.

rules.note: Compare 一月 yī yuè (January, a number name) with 一个月 yí ge yuè (one month, counting). Digit strings such as years also use yī; in phone and room numbers 一 is often read yāo instead.

rules.rule: Between a repeated one-syllable verb, 一 is light and toneless.

examples.py: nǐ kàn yi kàn zhè běn shū
examples.en: Have a look at this book.
Please wait a bit.
I'd like to give it a try.

rules.note: 等一下 is not this pattern: there 一 counts 下 and is yí xià.

rules.rule: Two 3rd tones side by side: say the first one as a rising 2nd tone. The pinyin spelling keeps both 3rd-tone marks; only the sound changes.

examples.en: Hello! (said ní hǎo)

examples.py: zhè r kě yǐ zuò ma
examples.en: May I sit here? (可以 said ké yǐ)
He loves eating fruit. (水果 said shuí guǒ)
I'd like some tea. (我想 said wó xiǎng)

rules.note: The change needs the two syllables to be said together. Across a comma or a real pause the first one keeps its 3rd tone.

rules.rule: With three or more 3rd tones, split the run into words or phrases first. Inside each group every 3rd tone before another 3rd rises; the last 3rd tone before a pause never changes.

examples.en: The boss came too. (老板也 said láo bán yě)
I'm fine. (said low wǒ + hén hǎo, or wó hén hǎo when fast)
I have five books. (said wó yǒu, wú běn)

rules.note: This is genuinely variable: speed and emphasis change the grouping, and in fast speech everything but the last syllable may rise. The fixed points are that a pair inside one word changes and the final 3rd tone stays.

rules.rule: Before a 1st, 2nd, 4th or neutral syllable a 3rd tone is just low: it dips and stays down, with no rise at the end. It does not become a 2nd tone.

examples.en: The teacher is busy. (老 and 很 stay low)
I like dancing. (我喜 said wó xǐ, 喜 low before 欢; 舞 full 3rd at the end)
Look, it's raining. (你 low before 看, 雨 low before 了)

rules.note: The full dip-and-rise 3rd tone is only heard on a word said alone or right before a pause. Mid-sentence, think 'low tone'.

rules.rule: Grammar particles and the suffixes 子 and 们 are always light and short: no tone mark, and their pitch simply follows the syllable before.
rules.pattern: word + 的 / 了 / 吗 / 呢 / 吧 / 着 / 过 / 们 / 子 (light)

examples.py: tā men shì wǒ de péng you
examples.en: They are my friends.
Have you eaten?
Let's go.

examples.py: hái zi men zài wài miàn wán r ne
examples.en: The children are playing outside.

rules.rule: In doubled family words and doubled verbs the second syllable is light. Doubled measure words and adverbs (天天, 人人, 常常) keep both tones.
rules.pattern: AA: tone + light (mā ma, xiè xie, kàn kan)

examples.en: Thank you, Mum.
Take a look at this.
Let me think. (said xiáng xiang)

examples.py: wǒ jiě jie tiān tiān pǎo bù
examples.en: My older sister goes running every day. (姐 low, 天天 both 1st tone)

rules.note: A doubled 3rd-tone verb still makes the first half rise (想想 xiáng xiang, 走走 zóu zou), but kin terms and 子 words do not: 姐姐, 奶奶, 椅子 are low + light.

contrasts.why: The mistake is in the sound: bù shì, with two falling tones. 是 is 4th tone, so 不 must rise: bú shì.
Said as bú hē by learners who make every 不 rise. 喝 is 1st tone, so nothing changes: bù hē. Only a following 4th tone triggers bú.

right.py: wǒ mǎi le yí ge shǒu jī

contrasts.why: Said as yī ge with the dictionary tone. 一 counting something before 个 is always yí, even though 个 itself is said lightly.

right.py: wǒ men yì qǐ chī fàn ba

contrasts.why: Said as yī qǐ or, by analogy with yí ge, as yí qǐ. 起 is 3rd tone, so 一 falls: yì qǐ. Rising yí is only for a following 4th tone.

right.py: jīn tiān shì shí yī yuè yī hào
right.en: Today is the first of November.

contrasts.why: Said as shí yí yuè yí hào because 月 and 号 are 4th tone. In month names and dates 一 is a number name and stays yī.
Said as dì yí kè. After 第 the 一 is an ordinal and keeps yī even before a 4th tone. Compare 一课 on its own counting lessons: yí kè.
Said with two full dipping tones, which sounds slow and foreign. The first of two 3rd tones rises: ní hǎo ma. The spelling stays nǐ hǎo.
Said as hén máng, over-applying the rising change, or with a full dip-and-rise on 老 and 很. Before a 1st or 2nd tone a 3rd tone just stays low.

right.py: wǒ yǒu liǎng ge gē ge

contrasts.why: Said as gē gē with two full high tones. In doubled family words the second syllable is light: gē ge. The measure word 个 is light too.
Said with a heavy, stressed bù as if 不 were the main word. Between a verb and its result 不 is quick and light: tīng bu dǒng.

cheat: 不 + 4th tone → bú. Before anything else, or alone → bù.
一 + 4th tone or 个 → yí. 一 + 1st / 2nd / 3rd tone → yì.
一 as a number name (counting, 第一, 十一, 一月, 一号, 星期一, end of phrase) → yī, whatever follows.
Two 3rd tones together: the first rises like a 2nd tone. The spelling does not change.
Three or more 3rd tones: group by words, raise the first of each pair, keep the last one as 3rd.
3rd tone before a 1st, 2nd, 4th or light syllable: stay low, no rise, and not a 2nd tone.
Particles, 子 / 们, doubled kin words and verbs (妈妈, 看看), middle 不 / 一 (好不好, 看一看): light.
